abstract.en: A single failed prediction can strike down an idea that survived a century.
abstract.cn: 一个失败的预测，就能打倒一个熬过百年的想法。

examples.en: The study refutes the claim that screen time alone lowers grades.
examples.cn: 这项研究驳斥了「仅靠屏幕时间就会降低成绩」的说法。

examples.en: He refused to comment before officials had refuted the report.
examples.cn: 在官方辟谣之前，他拒绝置评。

examples.en: A good theory makes itself refutable by predicting what will happen.
examples.cn: 好的理论通过预测未来而让自己可被证伪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「日肺图」——每天摊开肺部图，把香烟广告上的话一条条打回去，就是 refute 反驳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 refutare（击退、驳斥）→ 古法语 refuter → 英语 refute，其内部结构来源不确定；一般认为 re-（回）加一个表示「击打」的成分，核心动作是把论点打回去。

sensesIntro.en: Refute begins with proving a claim wrong, moves to denying a personal charge, then to experiment, debate, models, rumour, proof, and finally quotation.
sensesIntro.cn: refute 先指证明一个说法有误，再指否认针对个人的指责，然后延伸到实验、论辩、模型、传闻、证明，最后是引用他人的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat hand driving a spoken claim back to its speaker.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌把说出的话整个推回说话人面前。

branches.en: Proof: evidence, experiment, and logic all strike the same claim down.
branches.cn: 证明：证据、实验与逻辑都在打击同一类主张。

branches.en: Speech: a denied charge and a stopped rumour are words sent back without data.
branches.cn: 言语：否认指控与止住传闻，是不带数据的话语被送回去。

branches.en: Contest: in debate the claim belongs to an opponent, and the push-back wins the round.
branches.cn: 对抗：论辩中论点归对手所有，推回去就赢下一轮。

branches.en: Tools: a model or estimate is refuted when its output will not stand.
branches.cn: 工具：模型或估算产出站不住脚时就被推翻。

branches.en: Old rhetoric: another voice can do the striking, if it is quoted at the right moment.
branches.cn: 旧修辞：只要引用得法，另一个声音也能完成这一击。

intro.en: Refute is small but busy: re- back, the noun -ation, the adjective -able, and the negated irrefutable.
intro.cn: refute 词形短而活跃：re- 表示回，名词后缀 -ation，形容词后缀 -able，以及否定形式 irrefutable。

latinIntro.en: Latin refutare is the source. Its first element, re- “back”, is clear; the rest is of disputed or uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 refutare 是来源。第一个成分 re-「回」很清楚；其余部分的来历有争议或不确定。

items.example: Re- marks the backward push in refute.
items.exampleCN: re- 标记 refute 中往回推的动作。

items.meaningCN: 击退；制止；驳斥（拉丁语动词）
items.example: Refutare is the direct Latin source of refute.
items.exampleCN: refutare 是 refute 的拉丁语直接来源。

items.example: They refuted the paper in a single reply.
items.exampleCN: 他们用一篇答复就驳倒了那篇论文。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms the noun refutation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成名词 refutation。

items.example: His refutation ran to forty pages.
items.exampleCN: 他的驳斥长达几十页。

items.example: The suffix -able forms the adjective refutable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成形容词 refutable。

items.example: A refutable claim invites testing.
items.exampleCN: 可证伪的主张欢迎检验。

items.meaningCN: 不；非（否定前缀，加在 r 开头的词前）
items.example: The prefix ir- negates refutable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 把 refutable 变成否定。

items.example: The photos were irrefutable evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这些照片是无可辩驳的证据。

items.example: The suffix -er forms the rare noun refuter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成较罕见的 refuter。

definition_zh: 养生法；疗程方案；饮食起居制度；规律性做法；管理制度
definition_en: a fixed plan of living, eating, or treating an illness, followed with regularity
core_image: 墙上钉着一张表格，每天在同一时刻被同一支笔勾掉一行。
scene: 医生给她开了一套训练肺功能的日常方案，每天早晚各做一遍。The doctor prescribed a daily regimen of breathing exercises for her lungs.
sceneCN: 这里 regimen 是「日常方案、固定规程」（第 1 个义项：为健康而固定执行的一套做法）；句意：医生给她开了一套每日呼吸训练的日常方案。场景要点：诊室、打印的表格、被勾掉的一行行日子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 养生法；疗程方案；饮食起居制度；规律性做法；管理制度

derivatives.zh: 制度；政权；体系（与 regimen 同出 reigimen，现代多指政治或管理体系）
有关养生法或疗程的（-al 构成形容词，罕用）
严密编组；严格管制（源自同族 regiment，指把人按统一规则编排）
团；一大群；严格管控（同源词，强调统一指挥）

senses.title: A plan of living for health
senses.titleCN: 养生法：起居饮食的规程
senses.definition: a regular plan of food, sleep, and exercise followed to keep or improve health
senses.definitionCN: 为保持或改善健康而固定遵循的饮食、睡眠与运动计划
senses.example: He follows a light regimen of walking and early rising.
senses.exampleCN: 他遵循一套散步加早起的清淡养生法。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin regere “to rule”. A regimen is first the rule by which a body is governed each day.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于拉丁语 regere「统治」。regimen 最初指每天治理身体的那条规则。

senses.title: A medical course of treatment
senses.definition: a fixed schedule of drugs or therapy, with doses and times set out
senses.definitionCN: 药物或治疗的固定安排，写明剂量与时间
senses.example: The regimen requires three tablets after each meal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个疗程要求每餐后服三片药。
senses.why: When a rule governs an illness instead of a life, the regimen becomes a treatment schedule.
senses.whyCN: 当规则治理的是疾病而不是生活时，养生法就变成治疗时间表。

senses.title: A system of diet and exercise
senses.titleCN: 饮食训练制度：减重与体能
senses.definition: a strict set of rules on eating and training, often for weight or performance goals
senses.definitionCN: 关于饮食与训练的严格规定，常为减重或运动表现而设
senses.example: Athletes in camp share the same training and diet regimen.
senses.exampleCN: 集训的运动员遵循同一套训练与饮食制度。
senses.why: The training sense is a regimen that rules muscles and meals at once, and the rules are written down.
senses.whyCN: 训练义是一套同时管辖肌肉与饭食的方案，而规则是白纸黑字写下来的。

senses.title: Any fixed routine
senses.definition: any set of repeated habits that structures the day, from study to skincare
senses.definitionCN: 任何使一天有结构的重复习惯，从学习到护肤都算
senses.example: Her evening study regimen begins at eight and ends at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她的晚间学习常规从八点开始，十点结束。
senses.why: Once the word left medicine, any task that rules the day by the clock could be called a regimen.
senses.whyCN: 这个词离开医学之后，任何按时钟管住一天的任务都能叫 regimen。

senses.title: A rule or control
senses.definition: in older use, the act of governing, guiding, or controlling something
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中，指治理、引导或控制的行为
senses.example: The poem speaks of the regimen of the winds and tides.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗谈到对风与潮汐的支配。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: regimen named governing itself before it named governing a body.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：regimen 先指统治这件事，之后才指治理身体。

senses.title: An administrative order
senses.definition: a set of rules or an arrangement that governs an organisation or activity
senses.definitionCN: 管理某个组织或活动的一套规则或安排
senses.example: The university adopted a new regimen for research grants.
senses.exampleCN: 大学为研究经费采用了一套新规。
senses.why: Administration is ruling made visible in paper, so the noun slides from one to the other without a change of form.
senses.whyCN: 行政就是变成纸面可见的统治，所以这个词不用变形就从一边滑到另一边。

senses.title: A setting in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, the form or case that one word requires of another
senses.definitionCN: 语法中某个词要求另一个词采取的形态或格
senses.example: The regimen of the verb fixed the case of the following noun.
senses.exampleCN: 动词的支配关系决定了后面名词的格。
senses.why: Grammar is a set of rules too, so a word that demands a certain case is said to govern it.
senses.whyCN: 语法也是一套规则，所以要求某个格的词就被说成「支配」该格。

senses.title: Relative clause in climate science
senses.definition: in some technical writing, an older variant spelling of regime, as in a rainfall regimen
senses.definitionCN: 在某些技术文献中，是 regime 的较早异体拼写，如降雨型
senses.example: A wet rainfall regimen favours rice over wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 湿润的降雨型更利于水稻而非小麦。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the g that the popular medieval spelling inserted, so the older form survives as a variant.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义保留了中世纪口语拼写插入的那个 g，古老形式因此以异体存续。

intro.en: Regimen is Latin regimen, “rule, guidance”, from regere “to rule”. The same family gives regime, regiment, and English rule by way of Latin rulers.
intro.cn: regimen 就是拉丁语 regimen「统治、指导」，来自 regere「统治」。同一词族给出 regime、regiment，也经拉丁语统治者一词通向英语中的统治。

items.en: Regere meant “to keep straight, direct, rule”, from the same Indo-European root as regal and right.
items.cn: regere 意为「保持笔直、指引、统治」，与 regal、right 同出一个原始印欧语词根。

items.en: Regimen meant “a rule, a guidance”, and in medical writing a plan of diet and conduct for health.
items.cn: regimen 意为「规则、指导」，并在医学写作中指为健康而定饮食起居的计划。

items.en: A popular form reigimen, with a g inserted, travels in medieval medical Latin.
items.cn: 一种口语化形式 reigimen 插入了一个 g，在中世纪医学拉丁语中流传。

items.en: English takes regimen in the fifteenth century both as rule of conduct and as diet for health.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收了 regimen，既指行为准则，也指为健康而设的饮食。

items.en: Modern medical English settles on regimen for a prescribed routine of food, sleep, and treatment.
items.cn: 近代医学英语把 regimen 固定为规定的饮食、睡眠与治疗程序。

items.en: The word widens again to exercise regimens and study routines, while regime takes over the political sense.
items.cn: 该词又扩展到锻炼方案与学习常规，而政治上的「政权、制度」则由 regime 承担。

note.en: The first group is the words built on Latin regere “to rule”; the second marks neighbours that also name a plan you follow.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在拉丁语 regere「统治」之上的词；第二组标出同样表示「照着做的计划」的邻近词。

entries.definition: a government or system of rules. It grew beside regimen but took the political and technical senses.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或规则体系。它与 regimen 同源并行，却承担了政治与技术上的含义。

entries.definition: a large unit of soldiers, or to order people by strict rules. It keeps the image of ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 军队中的一大编制单位，或严加管束。它保留了「统治」的意象。

entries.definition: strict control over people and their behaviour. The noun of the verb to regiment.
entries.definitionCN: 对人及其行为的严格管控，是动词 regiment 的名词。

entries.definition: happening at fixed times and in a fixed pattern. It shares the ruling root of rule and regimen.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定时间与固定模式发生的。它与 rule、regimen 共享「规则」词根。

entries.definition: a usual order of doing things. It is looser than regimen and needs no medical purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 平时的做事顺序。它比 regimen 宽松，不一定要有医疗目的。

entries.definition: the food a person habitually eats, or a restricted plan of eating. It covers only food.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人常吃的食物，或受限的进食计划。它只管吃。

entries.definition: a fixed series of treatments or lessons with an end point. A regimen may go on indefinitely.
entries.definitionCN: 有终点的连续治疗或课程。而 regimen 可以一直持续下去。

entries.definition: official rules made by an authority. They govern people, while a regimen governs a body or a practice.
entries.definitionCN: 权力机构制定的正式规则。它们管人，而 regimen 管身体或一种做法。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin regere “to rule” plus the noun ending -men, giving regimen and its relatives regime, regiment, and regular.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 regere「统治」加上名词词尾 -men，得到 regimen，以及亲属词 regime、regiment、regular。

normal.en: Regimen comes from the same ruling root as regular: a regimen is what makes your days regular.
normal.cn: regimen 与 regular 同出「统治」词根：regimen 就是让你的日子变得规律的东西。

normal.en: Regimen is the body being ruled; regime is a country being ruled.
normal.cn: regimen 是被治理的身体，regime 是被统治的国家。

normal.en: In medicine, regimen means the dose and the clock, not just the drug.
normal.cn: 在医学中，regimen 指的是剂量加准时，而不只是药本身。

normal.en: The plural is usually regimens, though regimina appears in formal medical prose.
normal.cn: 复数通常是 regimens，正式医学文献里也会出现 regimina。

normal.en: Follow a regimen is the ordinary verb partner; put someone on a regimen is the phrase heard from the doctor.
normal.cn: follow a regimen 是常用动词搭配；put someone on a regimen 是医生的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a paper grid on the wall, one row crossed off at the same hour every day.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上有一张格子表，每天同一钟点被划掉一行。

abstract.en: A regimen is freedom bought in advance by giving up small choices for a while.
abstract.cn: 一套方案，是暂时放弃一些小的选择、预先买来的自由。

abstract.en: The body does not obey a wish; it obeys a calendar.
abstract.cn: 身体不服从愿望，它服从日历。

examples.en: Patients who followed the regimen for six months recovered faster.
examples.cn: 遵循该方案六个月的病人恢复得更快。

examples.en: Her morning regimen includes stretching, a cold shower, and two pages of reading.
examples.cn: 她的早晨常规包括拉伸、冷水澡和读两页书。

examples.en: Travellers often abandon their exercise regimen in the first week.
examples.cn: 旅行者往往在头一周就放弃锻炼计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞吉门」——瑞字贴的那道门上，每天同一时间开合一次，像一份作息规矩，就是 regimen 方案与养生法；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 regere（统治、指引，与 regal、right 同源）→ 拉丁语 regimen（统治；养生规程）→ 俗体 reigimen → 中古英语 regimen，核心是「按规则治理」，先治身，后泛指一切固定规程。

sensesIntro.en: Regimen keeps one idea, rule, and applies it to a body in eight ways: health, treatment, training, routine, governing, administration, grammar, and a technical spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: regimen 始终只有一个核心——规则，并在八个方向治理事物：健康、治疗、训练、常规、统治、行政、语法与一种技术性拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chart on the wall, one row crossed out at the same hour daily.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的表格，每天同一钟点划掉一行。

branches.en: Life: food, training, and study are all ruled by a schedule.
branches.cn: 生活：饮食、训练与学习都由时间表治理。

branches.en: Medicine: the same rule is imposed on an illness, dose by dose.
branches.cn: 医学：同一条规则被加在疾病上，一剂一剂地执行。

branches.en: Power: the original Latin “ruling” survives in governing and in administrative rules.
branches.cn: 权力：拉丁语原义的「统治」残留在治理与行政规章里。

branches.en: Grammar: a case demanded by a word is a small rule imposed by the verb.
branches.cn: 语法：由某个词要求的格，是动词加上的小规则。

branches.en: Climate: rainfall regimen keeps the older spelling alive in technical writing.
branches.cn: 气候：rainfall regimen 让较早的拼写在技术文献里保留下来。

intro.en: Regimen is a bare Latin noun: reg- “to rule” plus the ending -men. Its relatives are regime, regiment, regimentation, and regular.
intro.cn: regimen 是纯粹的拉丁语名词：reg-「统治」加词尾 -men。它的亲属词有 regime、regiment、regimentation 与 regular。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is regere “to rule” and regulator “director”; regimen means “a ruling”. The -men ending forms nouns of means or result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语核心是 regere「统治」与 regulator「指导者」；regimen 意为「统治之事」。词尾 -men 构成手段或结果名词。

items.meaningCN: 统治；使笔直（拉丁语词根）
items.example: The root reg- also stands in regular and regal.
items.exampleCN: 词根 reg- 也出现在 regular 与 regal 中。

items.example: Regere gives the ruling image behind regimen.
items.exampleCN: regere 提供 regimen 背后的统治意象。

items.example: Regimen was first medical, then general.
items.exampleCN: regimen 先是医学词，后成为一般词。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 动作的手段或结果（名词词尾）
items.example: The ending -men forms nouns from verbs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -men 把动词变成名词。

items.meaning: a fixed plan of living or treatment
items.example: The clinic posted a regimen by the door.
items.exampleCN: 诊所在门口贴了一份养生规程。

items.meaning: a system of government or of rules
items.example: Regime was the French spelling that won the political sense.
items.exampleCN: regime 是法语拼写，政治含义最终归了它。

items.meaning: a body of troops under one command
items.example: A regiment is a body of people ruled as one.
items.exampleCN: 一个团就是被当作一体治理的一群人。

items.example: The suffix -ment appears in regiment and regimentation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 出现在 regiment 与 regimentation 中。

items.example: The suffix -al forms the rare adjective regimenal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成罕用的形容词 regimenal。

items.meaningCN: 对人的严格编组与管制
items.example: The regime imposed strict regimentation on farmers.
items.exampleCN: 该政权对农民实行严格管制。

definition_zh: 倒退的；退步的；退化的；递减的；（税收）累退的
definition_en: moving backwards to an earlier or worse state, or becoming smaller as the amount rises
core_image: 一个人沿来时的脚印一步步往回走，身后的路越走越低
scene: 经济不景气时，一些家庭不得不把日子过得比十年前还节俭。In the downturn, several families had to accept a regressive way of life they thought they had left behind.
sceneCN: 这里 regressive 是「倒退的、退步的」（第 1 个义项：向更早或更差的状态回退）；句意为在经济下滑中，几户人家不得不接受一种他们以为早已抛在身后的倒退生活方式。

pos.zh: 倒退的；退步的；退化的；递减的

collocations.zh: 累退税（高收入者负担比例反而更低）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 regress 加名词后缀构成，义为「倒退；退回；回归」
由拉丁语 regredi 借入，义为「倒退；退回；回归」
同一词根的反义词，前缀 pro- 表向前，义为「前进；进步」
同一词根，前缀 ex- 表向外，义为「外出；出口」
同一词根，前缀 trans- 表越过，义为「越过；违反」

senses.title: Moving back to a worse state
senses.definition: going back to an earlier and less advanced or less fair condition
senses.definitionCN: 回到更早、更不先进或更不公平的状态
senses.example: Critics called the new rule a regressive step for workers.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称新规对工人而言是倒退的一步。
senses.why: The prefix re- sends the motion backwards, so a change can be measured as a step back rather than forward.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 把运动方向推向后方，因此一项变化可以被看成后退一步而不是前进一步。

senses.title: Shrinking as the amount grows
senses.definition: becoming a smaller share as income, price, or quantity increases
senses.definitionCN: 随着收入、价格或数量的增加，所占比例反而变小
senses.example: A flat sales tax is often described as regressive.
senses.exampleCN: 统一税率的销售税常被说成是累退的。
senses.why: A backward-moving rate still means a rate that runs against the rising amount, so economists use the same word for a shrinking share.
senses.whyCN: 「向后走」在这里指税率与增长的收入反向而行，经济学家便用同一个词指占比缩小。

senses.title: Returning to childish patterns
senses.definition: returning to the behaviour of an earlier stage of development, especially under stress
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在压力下退回到较早发展阶段的行为方式
senses.example: Under pressure, the child showed regressive behaviour again.
senses.exampleCN: 在压力之下，那个孩子又表现出退行性行为。
senses.why: Psychology applies the backward step to growth, so a person can move back to an earlier stage instead of forward.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把「后退一步」用在成长上，于是人可能退回较早的阶段而不是向前发展。

senses.title: Wearing away over time
senses.definition: of tissue or function, gradually wasting away or breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 指组织或功能逐渐萎缩、瓦解
senses.example: The scan showed regressive changes in the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示了组织的退化性变化。
senses.why: In medicine the backward path is a loss of full form, so tissue that loses strength is called regressive rather than progressive.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，「向后」意味着失去完整形态，所以逐渐失去强度的组织被称为退化性而非进展性的。

intro.en: Regressive is the adjective of regress, from Latin regressus, a going back, from regredi, to go back, built on re- back and gradi to step or walk.
intro.cn: regressive 是 regress 的形容词形式，regress 来自拉丁语 regressus（后退），源于 regredi（返回），由 re-（向后）与 gradi（迈步、行走）构成。

items.en: Gradi means to step or walk, and it underlies a whole family of motion words.
items.cn: gradi 意为迈步、行走，是许多表示运动词汇的共同基础。

items.en: Re- moves the walking backwards, giving regredi, to walk back.
items.cn: re- 把「走」的方向推到后方，构成 regredi，意为往回走。

items.en: The past participle and noun regressus name the return itself.
items.cn: 过去分词与名词 regressus 直接表示「返回」这件事。

items.en: English takes regress as a noun of returning; the exact first written date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 regress 作「返回」的名词；确切书面首见年代不确定。

items.en: The adjective form with the suffix -ive appears later, first as a technical term.
items.cn: 带 -ive 后缀的形容词形式较晚出现，最初用作术语。

items.en: Modern usage extends the backward step to taxes, psychology, and medicine.
items.cn: 现代用法把「后退一步」扩展到税收、心理学与医学。

note.en: Regressive is the adjective of the back-step root, so it sits beside regress, regression and progress, and near words for decline and decay.
note.cn: regressive 是「后退」词根的形容词形式，因此与 regress、regression、progress 相邻，也与表示衰退与腐蚀的词相邻。

entries.definition: to go back to an earlier state
entries.definitionCN: 倒退；退回（本词的动词来源）

entries.definition: a return to an earlier condition
entries.definitionCN: 倒退；回归（本词的名词形式）

entries.definition: movement forward to a better state
entries.definitionCN: 前进；进步（同词根，前缀 pro- 表向前）

entries.definition: towards an earlier or worse condition
entries.definitionCN: 向后的；落后的；在此处表示倒退的

entries.definition: gradually getting worse or weaker
entries.definitionCN: 下降的；衰退的

entries.definition: moving backwards or towards a worse state
entries.definitionCN: 倒退的；退化的（较正式）

normalIntro.en: Regressive keeps the walking root of gradi with a backward re-, so it is the adjective of a step taken in the wrong direction.
normalIntro.cn: regressive 保留 gradi 的「走」与 re- 的「向后」，因此它是「朝错误方向迈步」的形容词。

normal.en: Re- means back and gradi means walk, so regressive describes walking backwards.
normal.cn: re- 表向后，gradi 表行走，所以 regressive 描述的是往回走。

normal.en: A regressive tax charges the poor a larger share than the rich.
normal.cn: 累退税让穷人的负担比例高于富人。

normal.en: Opposite pair: regressive versus progressive, back step against forward step.
normal.cn: 反义成对：regressive 对 progressive，后退一步对前进一步。

normal.en: The verb regress and the noun regression share the same back-step idea.
normal.cn: 动词 regress 与名词 regression 共享同一个「后退」概念。

normal.en: Use regressive for systems, policies and behaviour, not for a single object moving.
normal.cn: regressive 多用于制度、政策与行为，而非单个物体在移动。

abstract.en: Picture footprints turning around and heading back down the hill.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印掉头，沿山坡往回走。

abstract.en: Picture a wide funnel narrowing as the numbers get bigger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽漏斗，数字越大反而越窄。

abstract.en: Picture an adult curling up like a child when things go wrong.
abstract.cn: 想象事情出错时，一个成年人像孩子一样缩起身子。

examples.en: Many economists call the flat fee regressive.
examples.cn: 许多经济学家认为固定收费是累退的。

examples.en: The reform was seen as a regressive move against small firms.
examples.cn: 这项改革被视为针对小企业的倒退之举。

examples.en: Teachers watched for regressive behaviour after the move.
examples.cn: 搬家和转学之后，老师们留意着退行性行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞格瑞西弗」——格里格往回走一步，台阶变矮：倒退、递减；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ gradi（迈步、行走）→ regredi（往回走）→ regressus（返回）→ 英语 regress → regressive，核心义「往回迈步」。

sensesIntro.en: Regressive begins with the social sense of a backward step, then narrows to a shrinking share, a return to earlier behaviour, and finally a medical wasting away.
sensesIntro.cn: regressive 先指社会意义上的「退后一步」，再收窄为占比递减，接着指退回较早的行为方式，最后指医学上的退化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footsteps turning around and walking back down the slope.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚印掉头，沿着斜坡往回走。

branches.en: THE BACKWARD STEP: a change that lowers a society or a rule to an earlier level.
branches.cn: 后退的一步：把社会或规则降回更早水平的变化。

branches.en: THE OPPOSITE SLOPE: the rate moves against rising income and so shrinks as a share.
branches.cn: 反向的坡度：税率与上涨的收入反向而行，因此占比缩小。

branches.en: THE CHILD AGAIN: a person returns to an earlier stage of behaviour under stress.
branches.cn: 又变回孩子：人在压力下退回较早的行为阶段。

branches.en: THE WORN TISSUE: in medicine the backward path means gradual wasting away.
branches.cn: 磨损的组织：在医学里，「向后」意味着逐渐萎缩。

branches.en: Both the social and the tax senses measure a movement against the expected forward direction.
branches.cn: 社会义与税收义都在拿实际变化与预期的前进方向作对照。

intro.en: Regressive is built on the walking root gradi with the backward prefix re- and the adjective suffix -ive.
intro.cn: regressive 由表行走的词根 gradi、表向后的前缀 re- 与形容词后缀 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin regredi means to go back, and regressus means a return; the -ive suffix turns that return into a quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regredi 意为返回，regressus 意为「返回」；-ive 后缀把这种返回变成一种性质。

items.example: Re- turns walking into walking back.
items.exampleCN: re- 让「走」变成「往回走」。

items.example: Gradi gives the family of movement words.
items.exampleCN: gradi 提供了一整族表示运动的词。

items.example: Regredi is the source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: regredi 是英语动词的来源。

items.example: Regressus gives the English noun regress.
items.exampleCN: regressus 给出英语名词 regress。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms regressive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 regressive。

items.example: Progress replaces re- with pro-, for forward.
items.exampleCN: progress 把 re- 换成表示向前的 pro-。

items.meaning: a return to an earlier state
items.example: Regression keeps the noun form of the return.
items.exampleCN: regression 保留「返回」的名词形式。

items.example: Regressive describes a backward change.
items.exampleCN: regressive 描述向后的变化。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms regressively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 regressively。

definition_zh: 规律性；规则性；整齐；匀称
definition_en: the quality of happening or being arranged in a fixed, repeated, or even way
core_image: 一把刻度均匀的尺子，每一格之间的距离完全相同
scene: 老街上的钟每天在同一时刻敲响，从未偏差。Passengers set their watches by the clock on the square, trusting its regularity for many years.
sceneCN: 这里 regularity 是「规律性」（第 1 个义项：按固定间隔重复出现的性质）；句意为乘客们照着广场上的钟对表，多年来一直信任它的规律性。

pos.zh: 规律性；规则性；整齐；匀称

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词来源，由拉丁语 regularis 借入，义为「规律的；规则的」
同一词根加动词后缀构成，义为「调节；管理」
由动词 regulate 加名词后缀构成，义为「规则；调节」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「调节器；监管者」
前缀 in- 变异为 ir- 表否定，义为「不规则；不正常」

senses.title: The quality of repeating at even intervals
senses.definition: the quality of happening again and again at fixed times or spaces
senses.definitionCN: 以固定时间或间隔反复发生的性质
senses.example: Gardeners rely on the regularity of the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁们依赖雨季的规律性。
senses.why: The noun of regular names the rule holding a rhythm together, so a repeated event has regularity.
senses.whyCN: regular 的名词形式指维系节奏的那条规则，因此反复发生的事就具有规律性。

senses.title: Evenness of shape or arrangement
senses.definition: the state of being evenly spaced, balanced, or orderly in form
senses.definitionCN: 间距均匀、平衡或形态整齐的状态
senses.example: The regularity of the stones surprised the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 石碑排列的整齐程度让参观者惊讶。
senses.why: A ruler that measures the same gap everywhere also describes shapes, so the word moves from time to visual evenness and order.
senses.whyCN: 刻度处处相同的尺子也能描述形状，于是这个词从时间转向视觉上的均匀与秩序。

senses.title: Conformity to a rule
senses.definition: the condition of following an established rule, standard, or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 遵循既定规则、标准或程序的状态
senses.example: Inspectors check the regularity of the paperwork.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员核查文件是否符合规定。
senses.why: Because regula means a rule, regularity can be used in institutions to mean that the proper procedure has been followed.
senses.whyCN: regula 本义是「规则」，所以 regularity 在机构语境中可表示按正当程序办事。

senses.title: Order in an unbroken series
senses.definition: a predictable pattern that a series of numbers or events follows
senses.definitionCN: 数列或事件序列所遵循的可预测模式
senses.example: The teacher asked students to find the regularity in the series.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让学生找出数列中的规律。
senses.why: Science and maths treat the repeated rule of regular as observable pattern, so a hidden order across a whole series counts as regularity.
senses.whyCN: 科学与数学把 regular 的「重复规则」看成可观察的模式，因此一整个序列背后的隐含秩序也算规律性。

intro.en: Regularity comes from Latin regularitas, from regularis, from regula, a straight stick used as a rule, and ultimately regere, to rule or guide straight.
intro.cn: regularity 来自拉丁语 regularitas，源于 regularis，再源于 regula（作直尺用的直棍），最终源于 regere（统治、使直）。

items.en: Regere means to rule, to guide, or to keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为统治、引导或使保持笔直。

items.en: Regula is a small straight rod, thus a carpenter rule and later a standard.
items.cn: regula 是一根小直棍，因此既指木匠的尺，也引申为准则。

items.en: The adjective regularis means of a rule, and so according to rule and even.
items.cn: 形容词 regularis 意为「合乎尺子的」，引申为依规则而行、均匀的。

items.en: The abstract noun regularitas names the quality of following the rule.
items.cn: 抽象名词 regularitas 指「符合规则」这一性质。

items.en: French passes the adjective and the quality into Middle English forms; the exact borrowing date is uncertain.
items.cn: 法语把形容词与这一性质传成中古英语形式；确切借入年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the everyday sense of a steady rhythm and the technical sense in maths and science.
items.cn: 现代英语既保留「稳定节奏」的日常义，也保留数学与科学中的技术义。

note.en: Regularity is the noun of the rule family, so it sits beside regular, regulate and regulation, and near words for rhythm, order and pattern.
note.cn: regularity 是「规则」词族的名词，因此与 regular、regulate、regulation 相邻，也与表示节奏、秩序与模式的词相邻。

entries.definition: happening at fixed intervals
entries.definitionCN: 有规律的；定期的（本词的形容词来源）

entries.definition: to control by rule
entries.definitionCN: 调节；按规则管理

entries.definition: lack of evenness or rule
entries.definitionCN: 不规则；反常（加否定前缀构成）

entries.definition: a repeated pattern of movement or sound
entries.definitionCN: 节奏；律动

entries.definition: the quality of being tidy and well arranged
entries.definitionCN: 井然有序；整洁

entries.definition: the quality of staying the same in behaviour or standard
entries.definitionCN: 一贯性；一致性

normalIntro.en: Regularity carries the Latin regula, a carpenter rule, so the word always measures whether things line up with the standard.
normalIntro.cn: regularity 带着拉丁语 regula（木匠的尺）的影子，因此这个词始终在衡量事物是否与标准对齐。

normal.en: Regula means rule, so regularity is the state of following a rule.
normal.cn: regula 意为规则，所以 regularity 是「合乎规则」的状态。

normal.en: The phrase with regularity means often or at steady intervals.
normal.cn: 搭配 with regularity 表示经常或按固定间隔。

normal.en: Add ir- for the opposite: irregularity means breaking the pattern.
normal.cn: 加上否定前缀 ir- 得到反义：irregularity 即打破规律。

normal.en: Regular, regulate and regulation all keep the rule inside them.
normal.cn: regular、regulate、regulation 都把「规则」藏在词里。

normal.en: Use regularity for time and space, consistency for opinions and behaviour.
normal.cn: regularity 多用于时间与空间，consistency 多用于意见与行为。

abstract.en: Picture a clock ticking at exactly the same beat, day after day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟日复一日以完全相同的节拍走动。

abstract.en: Picture rows of tiles laid with the same gap between each one.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排瓷砖，每块之间的缝隙宽度相同。

abstract.en: Picture an inspector running a finger along a straight edge.
abstract.cn: 想象检查员用手指沿一条直边滑过，确认是否笔直。

examples.en: The doctor noted the regularity of her heartbeat.
examples.cn: 医生注意到了她心跳的规律性。

examples.en: He visits his mother with regularity every Sunday.
examples.cn: 他每个周日都会按时去看望母亲。

examples.en: Scientists long suspected a regularity behind the tides.
examples.cn: 科学家早就怀疑潮汐背后存在某种规律。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞格尤拉瑞提」——拉一根直尺比一比，处处间距相同：规律、整齐；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 regere（统治、使直）→ regula（直尺；规则）→ regularis（合乎规则的）→ regularitas（规则性）→ 英语 regularity，核心义「与尺子对齐」。

sensesIntro.en: Regularity starts with repetition at even intervals, widens to visual evenness, then to following a rule, and finally to the hidden pattern of a series.
sensesIntro.cn: regularity 先指按均匀间隔重复，再扩展到视觉上的匀称，接着指遵循规则，最后指序列背后的隐含模式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler with perfectly even marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻度均匀的尺子。

branches.en: THE STEADY BEAT: an event returns at even intervals, as if measured by a ruler in time.
branches.cn: 稳定的节拍：事件按均匀间隔再次出现，像被一把时间的尺子量过。

branches.en: THE EVEN LINE: the same measuring idea moves from time into the arrangement of shapes and objects.
branches.cn: 均匀的线条：同一种丈量思路从时间转到形状与物件的排列上。

branches.en: THE RULE KEPT: institutions turn the ruler into procedure, so regularity means the correct form was followed.
branches.cn: 守住规则：机构把尺子变成程序，于是 regularity 表示按正确形式办事。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN PATTERN: in a series the rule must be discovered rather than seen, so regularity becomes an abstract law.
branches.cn: 隐藏的模式：在序列里规则要靠发现而不是靠看见，于是 regularity 成了抽象法则。

branches.en: A steady beat and an even row both depend on keeping a constant distance between items.
branches.cn: 稳定节拍与整齐排列都依赖保持各项之间恒定的间距。

intro.en: Regularity is built on the Latin rule regula, with the suffix -ity naming the quality and ir- able to negate it.
intro.cn: regularity 建立在拉丁语「规则」regula 之上，后缀 -ity 表示性质，前缀 ir- 可以把它变成否定。

latinIntro.en: Latin regula means a straight rod and then a rule, and regularitas means accordance with that rule.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 本指一根直棍，后指规则；regularitas 意为「与规则相符」。

items.example: Regere gives the sense of keeping on course.
items.exampleCN: regere 提供「保持在正道上」的含义。

items.example: Regula supplies the measuring stick.
items.exampleCN: regula 提供那把量尺。

items.example: Regularis becomes the English regular.
items.exampleCN: regularis 演变为英语 regular。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms regularity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 regularity。

items.example: Ir- negates regular to give irregular.
items.exampleCN: ir- 否定 regular，构成 irregular。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms regulate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 regulate。

items.example: Regulation keeps the family of rules together.
items.exampleCN: regulation 把一整套规则维系在一起。

items.meaning: a device or person that controls
items.example: Regulator names the controlling agent.
items.exampleCN: regulator 指起控制作用的一方。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms regularly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 regularly。

definition_zh: 反刍；反胃吐出；机械地重复；不加消化地照搬
definition_en: to bring food back up from the stomach, or to repeat facts without understanding them
core_image: 一股东西沿着原路逆流而上，从胃里被推回嘴中
scene: 培训课上，学员被要求复述教材里的原话，却不许加入自己的理解。The new staff were told not to regurgitate the manual but to explain each rule in their own words.
sceneCN: 这里 regurgitate 是「不加消化地照搬、机械重复」（第 2 个义项：把读来的内容不经理解地照搬出来）；句意为新员工被告知不要照搬手册，而要用自己的话解释每一条规则。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「反刍；反流；机械复述」
同源词，与拉丁语表示「喉咙」的词相关，义为「汩汩作响」
同前缀同词根的少见词，前缀 in- 表向内，义为「大口吞下」
一般认为与同一喉部词根相关，义为「峡谷；塞饱」

senses.title: To bring swallowed food back up
senses.definition: of an animal, to bring partly digested food back from the stomach into the mouth to chew again
senses.definitionCN: 指动物把部分消化的食物从胃里送回口中再次咀嚼
senses.example: Cows regurgitate their food and chew it again.
senses.exampleCN: 奶牛把食物反刍上来，再咀嚼一遍。
senses.why: The Latin gurges is a whirlpool, so the food is shown turning back against its usual downward flow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gurges 意为「漩涡」，于是食物像漩涡一样逆着原本向下的路径回流。

senses.title: To repeat without understanding
senses.definition: to repeat words, facts, or ideas mechanically without processing them
senses.definitionCN: 机械地重复词语、事实或观点而不加消化
senses.example: Students who merely regurgitate notes rarely understand the topic.
senses.exampleCN: 只是机械照搬笔记的学生往往并不理解这个主题。
senses.why: From the bodily image the word spreads to ideas, which are paid out again exactly as they came in, without digestion.
senses.whyCN: 从身体意象延伸开去，这个词也用于观点：原样吐出来，中间没有经过消化。

senses.title: To eject what was swallowed
senses.definition: of a person, to bring back up what has been swallowed, often without vomiting effort
senses.definitionCN: 指人把吞下的东西返上来，常不费力呕吐
senses.example: The infant regurgitated a little milk after feeding.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿喂奶后吐出了一点奶。
senses.why: A normal baby or patient can send swallowed liquid back up, so the medical sense keeps only the upward return, not the chewing.
senses.whyCN: 婴儿或病人也可能把吞下的液体返上来，于是医学用法只保留「向上回流」，去掉「咀嚼」。

senses.title: To flow back out again
senses.definition: of machines or pipes, to send liquid or gas back to where it came from
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或管道把液体或气体送回原来的地方
senses.example: The old pump regurgitated water into the vent.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧泵把水回喷进通风口。
senses.why: Engineers borrow the animal image for any flow that turns around and comes back out the way it went in.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用动物的意象，指任何掉头并从原路返回的流动。

intro.en: Regurgitate is built from Latin re- back and a root generally connected with gurges, a whirlpool and also the throat, so the word pictures a swallowing that turns back.
intro.cn: regurgitate 由拉丁语 re-（回）与一般认为和 gurges（漩涡，也指咽喉）相关的词根构成，因此这个词描绘的是「吞咽又倒回」的画面。

items.en: Gurges is a whirlpool, and by extension a gulf or throat; the link is generally accepted.
items.cn: gurges 意为漩涡，引申指深渊或咽喉；这一关联一般认为可信。

items.en: A frequentative verb gurgitare means to flood, swallow, or pour, and the throat sense grows from it.
items.cn: 反复动词 gurgitare 意为泛滥、吞下或倾注，喉部的含义由此发展。

items.en: The prefix re- sends the swallowing back, giving regurgitare, to flood back or throw up.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 让「吞咽」倒转，构成 regurgitare，意为回流或吐出。

items.en: The word is recorded in medical and herbal writing, where the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 该词见于医学与本草文字，确切的首次使用情况不确定。

items.en: English borrows it in the sixteenth century, first for the body and soon for words.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入此词，先用于身体，很快转用于言辞。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the animal sense and the critical sense of repeating without thought.
items.cn: 现代用法既保留动物义，也保留「不动脑子复述」的批评义。

note.en: Regurgitate is the upward-flow verb of the whirlpool root, so it sits beside regurgitation and gurgle, and near words for vomiting and for repeating without thought.
note.cn: regurgitate 是「漩涡」词根中表示「回流」的动词，因此与 regurgitation、gurgle 相邻，也与表示呕吐和不动脑复述的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of bringing food back up
entries.definitionCN: 反流；反刍（本词的名词形式）

entries.definition: to make a low bubbling sound
entries.definitionCN: 汩汩作响（与喉咙、水流的词根同源）

entries.definition: to swallow greedily
entries.definitionCN: 大口吞下（同词根反方向的前缀，较少见）

entries.definition: to throw up the contents of the stomach
entries.definitionCN: 呕吐（比本词更强调用力）

entries.definition: to repeat words without understanding
entries.definitionCN: 鹦鹉学舌般地重复

entries.definition: to repeat what another has said
entries.definitionCN: 重复别人的话；随声附和

normalIntro.en: Regurgitate links the re- of return with a whirlpool root, so the word always means something going back up the way it came.
normalIntro.cn: regurgitate 把表示「返回」的 re- 与「漩涡」词根连在一起，因此这个词总指某物沿原路向上返回。

normal.en: The prefix re- means back, so the swallowing turns around.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示返回，所以「吞咽」掉转了方向。

normal.en: The noun is regurgitation, and the -ation ending shows the action.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 regurgitation，后缀 -ation 表示动作。

normal.en: To regurgitate facts is to repeat them with no understanding.
normal.cn: regurgitate facts 即不加理解地重复事实。

normal.en: Compare chew the cud, the everyday phrase for animals that do this.
normal.cn: 对比日常说法 chew the cud，指动物反刍。

normal.en: Vomit is violent and everyday; regurgitate is a little more technical or critical.
normal.cn: vomit 更用力也更日常；regurgitate 稍偏技术或带批评意味。

abstract.en: Picture a whirlpool that spins the water back to where it started.
abstract.cn: 想象一个漩涡把水卷回到起点。

abstract.en: Picture a student reading notes aloud like a machine, with no thought.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生像机器一样大声念笔记，全无思考。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe blocked so that water bursts back out of the inlet.
abstract.cn: 想象管道堵住后，水从进水口倒喷出来。

examples.en: Ruminants such as sheep regurgitate their food to chew it fully.
examples.cn: 羊这类反刍动物会把食物反刍上来充分咀嚼。

examples.en: A good essay argues rather than regurgitates the syllabus.
examples.cn: 好论文会进行论证，而不是照搬教学大纲。

examples.en: The baby will often regurgitate a little milk after a long feed.
examples.cn: 喂奶时间较长后，婴儿常常会吐出一点奶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞格杰泰特」——格杰把吞下的东西又送回嘴边：反刍、回吐，进而指不动脑照搬；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为拉丁语 gurges（漩涡；咽喉）→ gurgitare（倾注、吞咽）→ re- + gurgitare 构成 regurgitare（回流、吐出）→ 英语 regurgitate，核心义「吞下又倒回」。

sensesIntro.en: Regurgitate begins with the animal body sense of food coming back up, passes to repeated words, then to a patient bringing liquid up, and ends with machines that send liquid back.
sensesIntro.cn: regurgitate 从动物把食物返上来这一身体义出发，转向重复的话，再到病人把液体返上来，最后到机器把液体送回。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something swallowed turns back and flows up the throat again.
core.cn: 核心意象：吞下的东西掉头，沿咽喉再次向上涌出。

branches.en: THE COW AT GRASS: partly digested food rises to be chewed again, the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 吃草的牛：部分消化的食物升回口中再咀嚼，这是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE PARROTED NOTES: ideas come back out exactly as they went in, with no work in between.
branches.cn: 被鹦鹉学舌的笔记：观点原样吐出，中间毫无加工。

branches.en: THE FED INFANT: a person brings liquid up easily, so the medical sense drops the chewing part.
branches.cn: 喂过奶的婴儿：人轻易地把液体返上来，医学义因此只保留回流部分。

branches.en: THE BLOCKED PIPE: machines borrow the same image for flow that reverses direction.
branches.cn: 堵住的管道：机器借用同一意象，表示方向倒转的流动。

branches.en: Animal rumination and human reflux share one physical picture of food moving upward.
branches.cn: 动物的反刍与人的反流共享同一个「食物上行」的身体画面。

intro.en: Regurgitate is built with the return prefix re- and a whirlpool root, with -ate marking a verb and -ation its noun.
intro.cn: regurgitate 由表返回的前缀 re- 与「漩涡」词根构成，-ate 标记动词，-ation 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gurges means a whirlpool or throat, and re- adds the turning back; regurgitare means to flood back or throw up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gurges 意为漩涡或咽喉，re- 加上「回转」之意；regurgitare 意为回流或吐出。

items.example: Re- reverses the direction of swallowing.
items.exampleCN: re- 让「吞咽」的方向反转。

items.example: Gurges supplies the whirling image.
items.exampleCN: gurges 提供漩涡的意象。

items.example: Gurgitare is the frequentative form.
items.exampleCN: gurgitare 是反复动词形式。

items.example: Regurgitare is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: regurgitare 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ate marks the verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 标记动词。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms regurgitation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 regurgitation。

items.example: Ingurgitate points the flow the other way.
items.exampleCN: ingurgitate 把流动指向相反方向。

items.example: Gurgle keeps the water noise of the root.
items.exampleCN: gurgle 保留词根里水流的声音。

items.meaning: the act of bringing back up
items.example: Regurgitation names the upward return.
items.exampleCN: regurgitation 指向上回流这一动作。

definition_zh: 驯鹿；驯鹿的肉；驯鹿皮
definition_en: a large deer with branching antlers that lives in cold northern regions and is herded by people
core_image: 雪原上一群长着宽蹄、顶着分叉鹿角的鹿，拉着雪橇前进
scene: 北方的冬季又长又黑，生活在那里的人们靠养这种鹿、拉雪橇和剪下皮毛来维持生计。In the far north the reindeer grazed on frozen moss and pulled the sleds of the winter travellers.
sceneCN: 这里 reindeer 是「驯鹿」（第 1 个义项：生活在北方寒带的鹿）；句意：在极北之地，驯鹿啃食冻结的苔藓，并为冬季的旅人拉雪橇。

pos.zh: 驯鹿肉；驯鹿皮（作食材、材料时）

derivatives.zh: 以驯鹿为生的牧民，由 reindeer 加表示「放牧人」的 herder 构成
驯鹿苔，一种地衣，名称来自驯鹿冬季的主要食物
驯鹿角，分叉的大角，可作雕刻与药用材料
北美对同一动物群的称呼，与驯鹿为同一种群的不同叫法

senses.title: The northern deer
senses.definition: a large deer of cold northern regions with broad hooves and branched antlers
senses.definitionCN: 生活在北方寒冷地区、蹄宽、角分叉的大型鹿
senses.example: A herd of reindeer crossed the frozen lake at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一群驯鹿在黎明时穿过结冰的湖面。
senses.why: The name joins a word for the deer with a word meaning deer, so the animal is named by what the deer is.
senses.whyCN: 名称由一个表示「鹿」的成分与一个表示「鹿」的词合并而成，动物就是按「鹿」来命名的。

senses.title: The domesticated herd animal
senses.definition: the same animal when kept and herded by people for sledding, milking, or its hide
senses.definitionCN: 被人饲养、用于拉雪橇、挤奶或取皮的同一类鹿
senses.example: The family keeps two hundred reindeer on the high pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 这户人家在高处牧场上养着两百头驯鹿。
senses.why: Northern peoples tamed the animal centuries ago, so the wild name also names a herd animal.
senses.whyCN: 北方民族数百年前就驯化了这种动物，于是野生动物的名字也用来指家畜。

senses.title: The Christmas reindeer
senses.definition: the deer that pull the sleigh of Santa Claus in winter folklore
senses.definitionCN: 冬季民间传说中为圣诞老人拉雪橇的鹿
senses.example: Eight reindeer pull the sleigh through the snowy night.
senses.exampleCN: 八只驯鹿拉着雪橇穿过风雪交加的夜晚。
senses.why: The sled animal of the far north passed into winter storybooks as the partner of a gift bringer.
senses.whyCN: 极北的雪橇动物走进冬季故事书，成了送礼人的同伴。

senses.title: Reindeer meat
senses.definition: the meat of this animal, eaten in northern Europe and Siberia
senses.definitionCN: 这种动物的肉，在北欧与西伯利亚作为食物
senses.example: The restaurant serves reindeer with mashed potato.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐馆供应配土豆泥的驯鹿肉。
senses.why: Where the animal is herded, its flesh is everyday food, so the animal name also names the meat.
senses.whyCN: 在饲养这种动物的地方，它的肉是日常食物，所以动物名也用来指肉。

senses.title: Reindeer hide
senses.definition: the skin of the animal, used for warm clothing, boots, and bedding
senses.definitionCN: 这种动物的皮，用作保暖衣物、靴子和被褥
senses.example: Reindeer keeps out the cold better than sheepskin.
senses.exampleCN: 驯鹿皮比羊皮更能挡寒。
senses.why: The hollow hairs of northern deer hold warmth, so the hide became a valued material named after the animal.
senses.whyCN: 北方鹿的毛是中空的，能保暖，所以鹿皮成了以动物命名的贵重材料。

senses.title: The animal as a figure
senses.titleCN: 驯鹿（作为北方与荒野的象征）
senses.definition: the animal used as a symbol of northern wilderness and survival
senses.definitionCN: 被用作北方荒野与生存能力的象征
senses.example: The reindeer on the city crest stands for endurance.
senses.exampleCN: 城市徽章上的驯鹿代表坚韧。
senses.why: A creature that survives the long polar winter naturally stands for endurance and the far north.
senses.whyCN: 能度过极地漫长冬季的动物，自然成了坚韧与极北的象征。

intro.en: Reindeer seems to join an old Norse word for the animal with the Old English word for deer; the first part is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: reindeer 似乎由古北欧语中表示这种动物的词与古英语中表示「鹿」的词组成；前半部分的来源尚不确定。

items.en: Hreinn is the northern word for the animal.
items.cn: hreinn 是北方对这种动物的称呼。

items.en: Deor means a wild animal, and later a deer, so deer once covered any beast.
items.cn: deor 意为野兽，后来指鹿；古英语中 deer 可泛指一切动物。

items.en: Reindeer appears as a compound of the northern name and the native deer word.
items.cn: 中古英语中，reindeer 作为一个复合词出现，由北方名称与本土的 deer 合成。

items.en: Travel and trade with the far north spread the word across Britain.
items.cn: 与远北地区的旅行和贸易使这个词在英国传播开来。

items.en: Herds in Lapland and Siberia make the word standard in northern accounts.
items.cn: 拉普兰与西伯利亚的鹿群使这个词成为北方记述中的标准用词。

items.en: The folk tale of flying sleighs fixes the word in the winter imagination.
items.cn: 飞行雪橇的民间故事把这个词固定在冬日的想象里。

note.en: Reindeer belongs with deer, the northern herding words, and the caribou name used in North America.
note.cn: reindeer 与 deer、北方的放牧用语以及北美使用的 caribou 相邻。

entries.definition: an animal of the family with antlers, including reindeer
entries.definitionCN: 鹿类动物，驯鹿属于其中

entries.definition: a person who keeps and tends reindeer
entries.definitionCN: 饲养和照看驯鹿的人

entries.definition: a lichen eaten by reindeer in winter
entries.definitionCN: 驯鹿冬季食用的一种地衣

entries.definition: the North American name for the wild form of this deer
entries.definitionCN: 北美对同一种鹿的野生类型的称呼

entries.definition: a very large deer of northern forests
entries.definitionCN: 北方森林中的一种大型鹿（欧洲称 elk，北美称 moose）

entries.definition: a vehicle on runners drawn by animals over snow
entries.definitionCN: 由动物在雪上拉动的带滑橇的车辆

normalIntro.en: Reindeer is a deer of the snow: its two halves say animal and deer, so the name never loses the deer.
normalIntro.cn: reindeer 是雪地里的鹿：两个成分分别表示「动物」与「鹿」，所以名称始终不离开「鹿」。

normal.en: The rear half of the word is deer, the English word for the family.
normal.cn: 词的后半部分是 deer，就是英语的「鹿」。

normal.en: The first part comes from an old Norse name for the animal, not from rain.
normal.cn: 前半部分来自古北欧语对这一动物的称呼，与 rain（雨）无关。

normal.en: A reindeer herder is the standard phrase for someone who keeps the deer.
normal.cn: reindeer herder 是「驯鹿牧民」的标准说法。

normal.en: Reindeer moss is a lichen, so a reindeer may eat it in winter.
normal.cn: reindeer moss 是一种地衣，所以驯鹿冬天会吃它。

normal.en: Compare caribou, the North American name for the same animal.
normal.cn: 对比 caribou，那是北美对同一种动物的称呼。

abstract.en: Picture broad hooves spreading over snow like snowshoes.
abstract.cn: 想象宽大的蹄子像雪鞋一样铺在雪面上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope of deer tied in a line, each one pulling a sled.
abstract.cn: 想象一长串鹿被绳子系住，一只接一只拉着雪橇。

abstract.en: Picture eight deer tracing the outlines of a sky across the night.
abstract.cn: 想象八只鹿在夜空里画出飞行的轮廓。

examples.en: Reindeer survive the polar winter by eating lichen under the snow.
examples.cn: 驯鹿靠吃雪下的地衣度过极地冬季。

examples.en: Herders move their reindeer to new pasture as the seasons change.
examples.cn: 随着季节变化，牧民把驯鹿赶到新的牧场。

examples.en: In the story, a team of reindeer waited outside the door.
examples.cn: 在故事里，一队驯鹿等在门外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞恩·迪尔」——瑞雪里跑出的一只鹿，就是驯鹿；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为由古北欧语 hreinn（这种动物的北方名称）与古英语 deor（野兽，后指鹿）组合而成；hreinn 的词根来源不确定，reindeer 并非来自 rain（雨）。核心义「雪原上的鹿」。

sensesIntro.en: Reindeer first names the northern deer, then the herd animal, its meat, its hide, the winter storybook figure, and finally a symbol of the north.
sensesIntro.cn: reindeer 先指北方的鹿，再由它指驯鹿群、驯鹿肉、驯鹿皮、冬季故事里的形象，最后指作为象征的驯鹿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a herd of broad-hoofed deer walking across snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群宽蹄的鹿踏过雪原。

branches.en: The deer of the north is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 北方的鹿是字面义项。

branches.en: A tamed herd turns the wild name into livestock.
branches.cn: 被驯养的鹿群把野生动物的名字变成家畜。

branches.en: The sleigh animal of northern life becomes a festive figure.
branches.cn: 北方生活中的雪橇动物变成节日形象。

branches.en: Meat and hide name what the animal gives its herders.
branches.cn: 肉与皮指这种动物提供给牧民的东西。

branches.en: Both the animal and its emblem stand for northern survival.
branches.cn: 动物本身与它的标志含义都代表北方的生存能力。

intro.en: Reindeer is a compound whose halves name an animal and a deer, and it builds phrases such as reindeer herder and reindeer moss.
intro.cn: reindeer 是复合词，两个成分分别表示「动物」与「鹿」，并构成 reindeer herder、reindeer moss 等短语。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from Old Norse rather than Latin, so the Latin entries here are only related relatives such as cervus for a deer.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自古北欧语而非拉丁语，所以这里的拉丁同源词只是相关亲戚，如表示鹿的 cervus。

items.example: Hreinn was the northern name for the animal.
items.exampleCN: hreinn 是北方人对这种动物的称呼。

items.example: Deor once meant any wild animal.
items.exampleCN: deor 原本泛指任何野兽。

items.example: Deer narrowed from all beasts to one family.
items.exampleCN: deer 从泛指野兽缩小为指鹿科动物。

items.example: Reindeer keeps both halves visible.
items.exampleCN: reindeer 的两个成分都还看得出。

items.example: The suffix -er forms herder.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 herder。

items.example: Herder pairs with reindeer in reindeer herder.
items.exampleCN: herder 与 reindeer 组成 reindeer herder。

items.example: Moss in reindeer moss is really a lichen.
items.exampleCN: reindeer moss 里的 moss 其实是地衣。

items.example: A reindeer herder follows the herd all year.
items.exampleCN: 驯鹿牧民一年到头跟着鹿群。

items.example: Reindeer moss covers the winter pasture.
items.exampleCN: 驯鹿苔覆盖着冬季牧场。

items.meaning: the North American name for the animal
items.example: Caribou is the North American twin of the word.
items.exampleCN: caribou 是这个词在北美的同类叫法。

definition_zh: 使恢复精力；使重新焕发活力；复兴
definition_en: to give fresh energy or strength to a person, group, or activity that has become weak
core_image: 一个人原本瘫坐，被扶起来后重新挺直腰杆、眼神发亮
scene: 一支乐队巡演熬了几个月，人人疲倦，唱片卖得也差；他们暂时停下休息，回到录音室重新找到了动力。A short break reinvigorated the players and their writing.
sceneCN: 这里 reinvigorate 是「使重新充满活力」（第 1 个义项：让疲惫的人或事物重获精力）；句意：短暂的休息让乐手和他们的创作重获活力。

pos.zh: 使恢复精力；使重新充满活力
使复兴；振兴（组织、经济、行业）

collocations.zh: 使疲惫的身体恢复气力

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词词尾 -ion 构成，义为「重振；恢复活力」
去掉前缀 re- 的基础动词，义为「使有活力；鼓舞」
加词尾 -ing 构成的分词形容词，义为「令人精神振作的」，如 invigorating air
过去分词作形容词，义为「重新振作的；恢复元气的」

senses.title: To give fresh energy back
senses.definition: to make a tired person or body feel strong and lively again
senses.definitionCN: 使疲惫的人或身体重新感到有力、有精神
senses.example: A week by the sea reinvigorated the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 在海边待了一周，全家人重新有了精神。
senses.why: The prefix re- means back or again, and invigorate means to fill with vigour, so the word restores energy to someone who has lost it.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「回、再」，invigorate 表示「注入活力」，所以这个词是把精力还给已经失去它的人。

senses.title: To revive an organisation or economy
senses.definition: to bring new strength and activity to an organisation, industry, or economy that has slowed down
senses.definitionCN: 使放缓的组织、行业或经济重新获得力量与活力
senses.example: The tax cut was meant to reinvigorate small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 减税的目的是让小企业重振旗鼓。
senses.why: The same image moves from a tired body to a sluggish system that needs its vigour restored.
senses.whyCN: 同一个意象从疲惫的身体，转到需要重新注入活力的迟缓体系。

senses.title: To renew interest or belief
senses.definition: to make interest, belief, or a discussion lively again
senses.definitionCN: 使兴趣、信念或讨论重新活跃起来
senses.example: The lecture reinvigorated my interest in the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座重新点燃了我对这门学科的兴趣。
senses.why: Interest can run down like strength, so giving it vigour again uses the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 兴趣也会像体力一样消退，所以「重新给它注入活力」用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: To restore the tone of a place
senses.definition: to fill a place, street, or community with new life and activity
senses.definitionCN: 使地方、街道或社区重新充满生气与活动
senses.example: New cafés have reinvigorated the old harbour district.
senses.exampleCN: 新开的咖啡馆让旧港口区重获生气。
senses.why: Places are described as tired, so a place can be given strength in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 地方也会被形容为「疲惫」，所以同样可以给它注入力量。

senses.title: To give the body new vigour
senses.definition: to make weak limbs or dull senses alert and strong again
senses.definitionCN: 使虚弱的肢体或迟钝的感官重新有力、灵敏
senses.example: Cold water reinvigorated his arms after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途攀登之后，冷水让他的双臂重新有了力气。
senses.why: This is the most physical use, close to the original sense of vigour as bodily strength.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的用法，接近 vigour 原本「体力」的含义。

intro.en: Reinvigorate puts the Latin prefix re- in front of invigorate, which comes from Latin vigor and the verb vigere.
intro.cn: reinvigorate 是在 invigorate 前面加上拉丁语前缀 re-，而 invigorate 源自拉丁语 vigor 与动词 vigere。

items.en: Vigere means to be lively or flourish, and vigor means liveliness.
items.cn: vigere 意为「有生气、旺盛」，vigor 意为「活力」。

items.en: The verb invitare is sometimes suggested as a link, but this is uncertain.
items.cn: 有时会提到邀请义的动词 invitare 作为联系，但这尚不确定。

items.en: Invigorate enters English with the sense of filling someone with vigour.
items.cn: invigorate 进入英语，义为「给某人注入活力」。

items.en: Invigorate and its noun form spread through medical writing.
items.cn: invigorate 及其名词形式通过医学写作传播开来。

items.en: The prefix re- means back or again, so reinvigorate means to give vigour back.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「回、再」，所以 reinvigorate 意为「把活力还回来」。

items.en: Reinvigorate becomes common in politics and business talk, as in reinvigorating the economy.
items.cn: reinvigorate 在政治与经济话语中流行起来，如「重振经济」。

note.en: Reinvigorate sits between the plain word invigorate and the re- family that adds back, and it is close to refresh, revive, and revitalise.
note.cn: reinvigorate 站在基础词 invigorate 与表示「再」的 re- 家族之间，并与 refresh、revive、revitalise 意义相近。

entries.definition: to fill with vigour or energy
entries.definitionCN: 给……注入活力

entries.definition: making someone feel lively and strong again
entries.definitionCN: 令人重新振奋的

entries.definition: the act of restoring energy or strength
entries.definitionCN: 重振；恢复活力

entries.definition: physical strength and good health
entries.definitionCN: 活力；精力

entries.definition: to bring back into life, use, or activity
entries.definitionCN: 使复活；使恢复使用或活动

entries.definition: to make someone feel less tired or less hot
entries.definitionCN: 使清醒；使恢复精神

entries.definition: to make someone or something look or feel young again
entries.definitionCN: 使年轻；使恢复青春

normalIntro.en: Reinvigorate is a machine word: invigorate fills a machine with power and re- switches it back on.
normalIntro.cn: reinvigorate 是一个「复原」词：invigorate 给机器注入动力，re- 则表示重新开启。

normal.en: The base is invigorate, from vigour, so the word is about vigour coming back.
normal.cn: 基础词是 invigorate，源自 vigour（活力），所以这个词讲的是活力回来。

normal.en: The prefix re- marks the second time, not the first.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 标记的是「再一次」，而不是第一次。

normal.en: Reinvigorate the economy is a set phrase in news writing.
normal.cn: reinvigorate the economy 是新闻写作中的固定说法，意为「重振经济」。

normal.en: The noun is reinvigoration, formed with the suffix -ion.
normal.cn: 名词是 reinvigoration，由词尾 -ion 构成。

normal.en: Compare revive: revive starts something dead or stopped, while reinvigorate adds strength to something tired.
normal.cn: 对比 revive：revive 让已停止的东西复活，reinvigorate 是给疲惫的东西补回力量。

abstract.en: Picture a flat battery from a car being charged until the engine starts.
abstract.cn: 想象一块没电的汽车电瓶被充电，直到引擎重新启动。

abstract.en: Picture a wilting plant straightening after a long rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一株打蔫的植物在久雨后重新挺直。

abstract.en: Picture a tired crowd rising to its feet as new drums begin.
abstract.cn: 想象疲惫的人群随着新的鼓点重新站起。

examples.en: Two weeks of rest reinvigorated the exhausted climbers.
examples.cn: 两周的休息让疲惫的登山者恢复了精力。

examples.en: The mayor wants to reinvigorate the city centre with more trees and fewer cars.
examples.cn: 市长想用更多树木和更少车辆来振兴市中心。

examples.en: Her lecture reinvigorated my interest in marine biology.
examples.cn: 她的讲座重新激发了我对海洋生物学的兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞因·维格·锐特」——再（瑞）次一拉（因）就更有劲（维格），于是重新振作；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次、回）＋ vigor（活力，源自 vigere 有生气、旺盛）→ invigorate（注入活力）→ reinvigorate（重新注入活力）；有时提及 invitare 作中介，但这一说法不确定。核心义「把活力还回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Reinvigorate starts with a tired body, moves on to a sluggish economy or organisation, then to renewed interest, to a lifeless place, and finally back to bodily strength.
sensesIntro.cn: reinvigorate 从疲惫的身体出发，进而指迟缓的经济或组织，再到重燃的兴趣、重获生气的地方，最后回到身体力气本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slumped figure straightening up as energy flows back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个瘫坐着的人重新挺直腰板，力量流回身体。

branches.en: A tired person gets energy back.
branches.cn: 疲惫的人重新获得精力。

branches.en: A slow system gets strength again.
branches.cn: 迟缓的体系重新获得力量。

branches.en: Interest is treated as energy that can be renewed.
branches.cn: 兴趣被当作可以再充的能量。

branches.en: A place gets life when it gets activity.
branches.cn: 地方获得活动，也就重新有了生气。

branches.en: The body sense is the literal root of all the others.
branches.cn: 身体义项是其他所有义项的字面根源。

intro.en: Reinvigorate is built from re-, the verb invigorate, and the Latin root vigor; the suffix -ion and -ing extend the family.
intro.cn: reinvigorate 由前缀 re-、动词 invigorate 与拉丁词根 vigor 构成，词尾 -ion 和 -ing 又扩展出同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vigor means liveliness, and the verb vigere means to be strong or flourish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vigor 意为活力，动词 vigere 意为强健、旺盛。

items.example: The prefix re- turns invigorate into reinvigorate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把 invigorate 变成 reinvigorate。

items.example: Vigor is the noun behind the word.
items.exampleCN: vigor 是这个词背后的名词。

items.example: Vigere gives the idea of flourishing.
items.exampleCN: vigere 提供了「旺盛」的意思。

items.example: Vigour is the British spelling of vigor.
items.exampleCN: vigour 是 vigor 的英式拼法。

items.example: Invigorate adds -ate to the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: invigorate 在拉丁词根后加 -ate。

items.example: Reinvigorate keeps the whole base verb.
items.exampleCN: reinvigorate 保留了整个基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -ate makes invigorate a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 使 invigorate 成为动词。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms reinvigoration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 reinvigoration。

items.example: Reinvigoration names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: reinvigoration 指整个过程。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示效果的形容词
items.example: The suffix -ing forms reinvigorating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 reinvigorating。

definition_zh: 重申；反复说；再强调
definition_en: to say something again, or to say it once more in order to make it clear or firm
core_image: 同一句提示牌被人举起两次：第一次是提醒，第二次是强调
scene: 老师在黑板上写下规则，念了一遍，看学生没反应，又用更慢的语速把它说了一遍。She reiterated the rule about phones before the exam began.
sceneCN: 这里 reiterate 是「重申」（第 1 个义项：为了强调而再说一次）；句意：考试开始前，她又把关于手机的规定重申了一遍。

pos.zh: 反复强调（立场、承诺、要求）

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词词尾 -ion 构成，义为「重申；重复」
加词尾 -ive 构成，义为「重复的；反复的」
去掉前缀 re- 的基础动词，义为「重复说；迭代」
由 iterate 加 -ive 构成，义为「反复的；迭代的」，常见于程序设计
过去分词作形容词，义为「被反复说的；重申过的」

senses.title: To say again for emphasis
senses.definition: to say the same thing again so that the point is clear or remembered
senses.definitionCN: 把同一件事再说一次，使观点更清楚或更容易被记住
senses.example: The teacher reiterated the deadline at the end of the class.
senses.exampleCN: 下课前老师又重申了一次截止时间。
senses.why: Re- means again and iterate comes from Latin iterum, again, so the word means to say a thing a second time.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示「再一次」，iterate 来自拉丁语 iterum（又一次），所以这个词就是把话说第二遍。

senses.title: To stress a firm position
senses.definition: to state a position, promise, or warning firmly because it matters a great deal
senses.definitionCN: 立场、承诺或警告很重要，因而坚定地再声明一次
senses.example: The minister reiterated that no troops would be sent.
senses.exampleCN: 部长重申不会派出任何军队。
senses.why: A repeated statement of this kind is a public signal of firmness, so the verb takes on a formal weight.
senses.whyCN: 这类重复表态是公开表明坚定的信号，所以这个动词带有正式分量。

senses.title: To repeat because the listener missed it
senses.definition: to say words again because they were not heard, understood, or obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 因为别人没听到、没听懂或没有照做而把话再说一次
senses.example: He reiterated the name slowly so that everyone could write it down.
senses.exampleCN: 他慢慢地把名字又说了一遍，好让大家都能记下来。
senses.why: The plain idea of a second telling covers everyday cases where the first saying was not enough.
senses.whyCN: 「说第二遍」这一基本含义涵盖了第一次没说清楚的日常情形。

senses.title: To repeat formally in writing
senses.definition: to state a clause or instruction again in a formal document
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文件里把某条条款或指示再写一遍
senses.example: The contract reiterates the safety rules already in the manual.
senses.exampleCN: 合同把手册里已有的安全规定又重申了一遍。
senses.why: A written rule is often restated to bind the reader, so the verb moves into official documents.
senses.whyCN: 书面规则常被重复写出以约束读者，于是这个动词进入正式文件。

senses.title: To keep the argument going by restating
senses.definition: to restate an argument in a debate in order to keep it in view
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中把论点再说一遍，让它在讨论中继续被看见
senses.example: The speaker reiterated the same evidence at every stage.
senses.exampleCN: 发言人在每个阶段都反复陈述同样的证据。
senses.why: Restating an argument is how a point is kept alive in a long discussion.
senses.whyCN: 在长时间的讨论中，重复陈述论点就是让观点继续存在的方式。

senses.title: The repeated statement itself
senses.titleCN: 重复的表述（作为名词化的动作）
senses.definition: the act of repeating a statement, often as a set phrase, as in a reiteration of a policy
senses.definitionCN: 重复陈述这一动作，常用于固定表达，如政策的重申
senses.example: The final paragraph is a reiteration of the main finding.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一段是对主要发现的重复陈述。
senses.why: English freely turns the verb into the noun reiteration to name the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以把这个动词直接变成名词 reiteration，用来指这一动作本身。

intro.en: Reiterate joins the Latin prefix re- with iterare, to do again, and both go back to iterum, meaning again.
intro.cn: reiterate 把拉丁语前缀 re- 与 iterare（重做）结合在一起，二者都可以追溯到 iterum，意为「再一次」。

items.en: Iterare means to do a thing twice or repeat it.
items.cn: iterare 意为「做两次、重复」。

items.en: Iterum, a form of the comparative idea again, stands behind the verb.
items.cn: iterum 表达「再一次」的比较意味，是这个词背后的来源。

items.en: Medieval and school Latin use reiterare for repeating words or actions.
items.cn: 中世纪与学校用的拉丁语用 reiterare 表示重复言辞或动作。

items.en: Reiterate is recorded in English with the sense of doing or saying again.
items.cn: 英语中已见 reiterate，义为「再做或再说一次」。

items.en: The verb becomes common in preaching and law, where repetition carries weight.
items.cn: 这个动词在布道与法律中用得很多，因为在那里重复自有分量。

items.en: Modern usage keeps reiterate for formal repetition of a point or promise.
items.cn: 现代用法保留 reiterate 专指正式地重复要点或承诺。

note.en: Reiterate is part of a family of words about doing or saying again; its look-alikes are the iterate family, and its near meanings are the plain repeating verbs.
note.cn: reiterate 属于一组表示「再做一次、再说一次」的词；形近同族的是 iterate 家族，近义的是普通的「重复」动词。

entries.definition: to say or do something again, or to repeat a process
entries.definitionCN: 重复说；重复做（也指循环迭代）

entries.definition: the act of saying something again
entries.definitionCN: 重申；重复

entries.definition: expressing repetition
entries.definitionCN: 表示重复的

entries.definition: repeated, or involving a repeating cycle
entries.definitionCN: 反复的；迭代的

entries.definition: to say or do the same thing again
entries.definitionCN: 重复；再说一次

entries.definition: to say something again in a clearer or different way
entries.definitionCN: （更清楚地）重新陈述

entries.definition: to state a belief or promise firmly for a second time
entries.definitionCN: 再确认；重申信念或承诺

normalIntro.en: Reiterate is built from simple blocks: re- for again and iterare for doing it a second time.
normalIntro.cn: reiterate 由几个简单的部件搭成：re- 表示「再一次」，iterare 表示「做第二次」。

normal.en: Re- at the front means again, and the rest carries the sense of saying.
normal.cn: 词首的 re- 表示「再一次」，后面的部分承载「说」的意思。

normal.en: Remove re- and you get iterate, the base verb meaning to repeat.
normal.cn: 去掉 re- 就得到 iterate，是表示「重复」的基础动词。

normal.en: Reiterate a point is the phrase you hear in news reports.
normal.cn: reiterate a point 是新闻报道里常听到的说法。

normal.en: The noun is reiteration, formed with the suffix -ion.
normal.cn: 名词是 reiteration，由词尾 -ion 构成。

normal.en: Compare repeat: repeat is everyday, reiterate is formal and usually adds emphasis.
normal.cn: 对比 repeat：repeat 更日常，reiterate 更正式且通常带有强调意味。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler tapped twice on the desk to get the room to listen.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子在桌上敲了两下，让大家安静听讲。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed on the same line twice, making the ink darker.
abstract.cn: 想象印章在同一行上盖了两下，墨色变深。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher repeating a word until the whole class says it together.
abstract.cn: 想象老师把一个词重复说，直到全班一起说出来。

examples.en: The manager reiterated her concerns about the budget.
examples.cn: 经理重申了她对预算的担忧。

examples.en: Officials have repeatedly reiterated that the border remains open.
examples.cn: 官员们已多次重申，边境依然开放。

examples.en: Please reiterate the main points at the end of your talk.
examples.cn: 请在发言结束时重申主要观点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞·伊特·瑞特」——再说一遍，让听众再次（瑞）记住；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再一次）＋ iterare（重复、重做，源自 iterum「又一次」）→ 英语 reiterate；核心义「同一件事再说一遍」。

sensesIntro.en: Reiterate begins with saying something again for emphasis, then moves to a firm public restatement, to a plain repeat for a listener, to formal written restatement, to debate, and finally to the noun form.
sensesIntro.cn: reiterate 先指为强调而再说一遍，进而指郑重地公开重申、因对方没听清而再说一次、在文件中重复载明、辩论中的反复陈述，最后指名词化的重复表述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same sign held up twice, the second time more firmly.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一块提示牌被举起两次，第二次举得更用力。

branches.en: Saying the same thing again is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 把同一件事再说一遍是基本义项。

branches.en: A firm restatement of a position is the public sense.
branches.cn: 坚定地重申立场是公开语域中的义项。

branches.en: A repeat for a listener who missed it is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 为没听清的听众再说一次是日常义项。

branches.en: Documents repeat clauses and debaters restate points to keep them in view.
branches.cn: 文件重复条款、辩论者重复论点，都是为了让内容继续被看见。

branches.en: The noun reiteration names the act described by the verb.
branches.cn: 名词 reiteration 为动词所描述的动作命名。

intro.en: Reiterate is re- plus iterate; the Latin root iter means a going or a doing again, and suffixes -ion and -ive extend the family.
intro.cn: reiterate 是 re- 加 iterate；拉丁词根 iter 表示「行走、再做一次」，词尾 -ion 与 -ive 扩展出同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin iter means a journey and iterum means again, while iterare means to repeat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iter 意为行程，iterum 意为再一次，iterare 意为重复。

items.example: The prefix re- marks the second saying.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标记第二次说。

items.example: Iter gives the image of going over a path again.
items.exampleCN: iter 提供把路再走一遍的意象。

items.example: Iterum is the heart of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: iterum 是这个词意义的核心。

items.example: Iterare turns the adverb into a verb.
items.exampleCN: iterare 把这个副词变成动词。

items.example: Iterate is the verb without re-.
items.exampleCN: iterate 是去掉 re- 的动词。

items.example: Reiterate adds the idea that it is already known.
items.exampleCN: reiterate 加上「已经说过」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ate marks a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 标记动词。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms reiteration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 reiteration。

items.example: Reiteration names the repeated statement.
items.exampleCN: reiteration 指重复的陈述。

items.meaning: tending to, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ive forms reiterative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 reiterative。

definition_zh: 拒绝；退回；排斥；否定的回复；被拒绝的处境
definition_en: the act of refusing to accept, agree to or use something, or the state of being refused
core_image: 一封信被原封不动地推回桌面，封口都没拆
scene: 大学回信终于寄到，薄薄的信封里是一封拒绝信。The envelope held a polite letter of rejection from her first choice university.
sceneCN: 这里 rejection 是「拒绝」的名词（第 1 个义项：拒绝接受或答应某事）；句意：信封里是她第一志愿大学寄来的一封措辞礼貌的拒绝信。画面里那封被推回的信，正是核心意象。

pos.zh: 拒绝；退回；排斥；被拒绝的处境

derivatives.zh: 词根动词，义为「拒绝；退回」，名词 rejection 由它加 -ion 构成
由动词转成的名词，指「被拒收的次品或退回的货物」
形容词，义为「表示拒绝的；予以排斥的」

senses.title: The act of refusing a request or offer
senses.definition: the act of refusing to accept, agree to or take up something that is offered or asked for
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受、同意或采纳别人提出或请求的事情
senses.example: Their rejection of the proposal surprised the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对提案的否决让委员会大为意外。
senses.why: The root sense is to throw something back, so a refused request is literally sent back to the asker.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「往回扔」，被别人拒绝的请求就是被原样扔回提出者手里，所以最先长出的就是「拒绝」这个义项。

senses.title: A refusal to accept someone as a person
senses.titleCN: 被拒绝的处境；不被接纳
senses.definition: the experience of being refused acceptance by a group, a person or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 被群体、某个人或某个机构拒绝接纳时的处境与感受
senses.example: Rejection from the team left him quiet for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 落选球队让他沉默了好几周。
senses.why: When the object of the throwing back is a person rather than a thing, refusal becomes social exclusion.
senses.whyCN: 当被扔回去的对象从「东西」变成「人」时，拒绝就从对事的否决变成了对人或群体的排斥，于是延伸出「被拒于门外」的心理处境。

senses.title: A refusal to accept something submitted
senses.definition: an official refusal to accept a piece of writing, an application or goods that have been sent in
senses.definitionCN: 对送来审阅或呈交的稿件、申请或货物作出不予接受的正式决定
senses.example: The journal sent back a rejection within three days.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊在三天内寄回了退稿通知。
senses.why: Sending something back is the physical root of rejection, and publishers and editors keep exactly that picture.
senses.whyCN: 把东西退回是 rejection 最原始的画面，出版社与编辑沿用的正是这个动作，因此稿件被退回、申请被驳回都叫 rejection。

senses.title: Biological rejection of transplanted tissue
senses.definition: the response of a body or system that refuses to accept foreign tissue, a drug or a material
senses.definitionCN: 身体或某个系统对外来的组织、药物或材料不予接受而作出的反应
senses.example: Doctors watch closely for rejection after a transplant.
senses.exampleCN: 移植手术后医生密切关注排斥反应。
senses.why: The immune system literally refuses what is foreign and pushes it away, which is the throwing-back image moved inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 免疫系统对待外来物正是「不认、往外推」，核心的「扔回去」动作被搬进身体内部，于是医学上称器官移植失败为排斥。

senses.title: A thing that is refused as unfit
senses.definition: a product, part or specimen that is set aside because it fails a standard
senses.definitionCN: 因不达标准而被挑出、不予采用的成品、零件或样本
senses.example: The factory sells rejects and rejections at half price.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把次品按半价出售。
senses.why: Here rejection names the object thrown back, so the action word hardens into a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项里，rejection 直接去指「被扔回去的那件东西」，动作词因此物化成了具体名词，即被挑出来的次品。

senses.title: Refusal in engineering and psychology
senses.titleCN: 抑制；拒不接受（技术与人际）
senses.definition: in control systems, a device or study that keeps out unwanted input, such as noise, heat or a suggestion
senses.definitionCN: 在控制系统里指挡住不想要输入的装置或研究，如噪声、热量或他人的建议
senses.example: The filter allows good rejection of background noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这种滤波器能有效抑制背景噪声。
senses.why: Once an unwanted signal is treated as a thing to be refused, the word covers any mechanism that keeps it out.
senses.whyCN: 当不受欢迎的信号被当成「该被拒收的东西」时，任何把它挡在门外的机制都可以叫 rejection，于是扩展出工程与人际上的「抑制、不听劝」。

senses.title: Refusal within a legal or official procedure
senses.titleCN: 驳回；不予受理（法律与公务）
senses.definition: a formal decision by a court or office to refuse a claim, an appeal or an application
senses.definitionCN: 法院或政府机关对诉求、上诉或申请作出的不予接受或不予支持的正式决定
senses.example: The court upheld the rejection of his appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 法院维持了驳回其上诉的裁定。
senses.why: Legal usage keeps the underlying sense of refusing a thing offered, but fixes it to a recorded official act.
senses.whyCN: 法律用语保留了「拒收送来的东西」这一基础义，只是把随意的拒绝固定为作出书面记录、能写进卷宗的正式裁定。

senses.title: Rejection of a promise or belief
senses.definition: the act of declaring that something claimed or believed is false or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 宣布某种说法或信念为虚假或不可接受的行为
senses.example: Her rejection of the rumour was swift and firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她迅速而坚定地否认了那个传言。
senses.why: When a claim is offered as true, refusing to take it is also a rejection, so the word covers ideas as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 别人递过来的是一个「说法」，不接就等于把它扔回去，所以拒绝的对象从实物延伸到观念、传言与承诺，于是有了「否认、摒弃」。

intro.en: Rejection is the noun of refuse, formed in English from the Latin verb reicere, to throw back.
intro.cn: rejection 是动词 reject 的「-ion」名词形式，源自拉丁语动词 reicere（往回扔）。

items.en: *ye- is generally reconstructed as the root meaning “to throw”, seen in Latin iacere. The deeper origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语重构形式 *ye- 表示「投掷」，见于拉丁语 iacere；这个更深一层的来源不确定。

items.en: The compound reicere joined re- back with iacere to throw, meaning “to throw back, drive off, refuse”.
items.cn: 复合词 reicere 由 re-（向后）与 iacere（投掷）组成，意为「扔回去、赶开、不接受」。

items.en: The action noun reiectio, stem reiection-, named the act of throwing back or casting off; in English it is spelled rejection.
items.cn: 动作名词 reiectio（词干 reiection-）指「扔回、丢弃，或对事物的拒斥」；英语里写作 rejection。

items.en: The English verb came first through medieval Latin and Old French, recorded in English from the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先借入动词，经由中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入英语，名词 rejection 见于英语记载较晚，普及已在十七世纪。

items.en: Alongside the plain sense of refusal, the word gained technical senses in medicine, law and control engineering.
items.cn: 除了「拒绝」的本义，这个词又在医学、法律与控制工程中获得专业含义。

note.en: Rejection is the action noun of throwing back; it sits beside refuse, decline and refusal, and looks like injection and ejection.
note.cn: rejection 是把东西扔回去的动作名词，与 refuse、decline、refusal 属于同一义场，拼写上又与 injection、ejection 相近。

entries.definition: the verb that rejection is mainly built from
entries.definitionCN: 派生词根：rejection 主要由此动词加 -ion 构成，义为拒绝；退回

entries.definition: the act of forcing something out
entries.definitionCN: 同根不同前缀：与 rejection 共享 iacere（投掷）词根，意为「抛出、弹出」

entries.definition: the act of forcing liquid into something
entries.definitionCN: 同根不同前缀：词根同为 iacere，意为「注射、注入」，与「往外扔」方向相反

entries.definition: an act of saying no to something offered
entries.definitionCN: 近义：对别人的请求或提议说不，比 rejection 更中性和口语

entries.definition: to refuse politely an invitation or offer
entries.definitionCN: 近义：礼貌地婉拒邀请或提议，词性多为动词

entries.definition: an official decision to refuse a claim or argument
entries.definitionCN: 近义：法律上对诉求或论点的驳回，与第 7 个义项相邻

normalIntro.en: Rejection is throw back in noun form: re- means back, and the iac- root means throw.
normalIntro.cn: rejection 是「扔回去」的名词：re- 表示「向后」，词干 iac- 表示「扔」。

normal.en: Re- gives the backward direction in reject, as in return or reverse.
normal.cn: re- 在 reject 里表示「向后、回去」，同 return、reverse 的 re- 一样。

normal.en: The iac- root survives in eject and inject, all about throwing.
normal.cn: 词根 iac- 在 eject、inject 中都能看到，全都与「扔」有关。

normal.en: Reject is the verb and rejection is its action noun with -ion.
normal.cn: reject 是动词，加上 -ion 就成了表示动作的名词 rejection。

normal.en: A rejection letter is a letter that sends your application back.
normal.cn: a rejection letter 就是把你申请原样寄回的那封信：拒绝信。

normal.en: Doctors use rejection for the body refusing a transplant.
normal.cn: 医生用 rejection 描述身体对外来器官的「不接纳」，即排斥反应。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope sliding back across the desk to you.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没拆封的信封顺着桌面滑回你面前。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door shutting gently but firmly on someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在某人面前轻轻却坚决地关上。

abstract.en: Picture an editor with a stack of returned manuscripts.
abstract.cn: 想象一位编辑手边堆着一摞退回的稿件。

examples.en: Every rejection taught her to rewrite the opening paragraph.
examples.cn: 每一次退稿都让她学会重写开头段落。

examples.en: The risk of rejection is high and the cost is serious.
examples.cn: 发生排斥反应的风险很高，后果也很严重。

examples.en: His rejection of the offer ended the negotiation.
examples.cn: 他对报价的拒绝终结了这场谈判。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞杰克神」——被拒绝的提案被扔回桌上，像被一位神明当场拍板否决；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ iacere（投掷）→ reicere（扔回去；拒绝）→ 动作名词 reiectio → 英语 reject 与 rejection，核心义「把递来的东西推回去」。

sensesIntro.en: Rejection starts as the physical act of throwing something back and then spreads to people, manuscripts, transplanted organs, faulty products, signals and legal claims.
sensesIntro.cn: rejection 从「把东西扔回去」这个具体动作出发，再扩展到对人、对稿件、对移植器官、对次品、对信号以及对法律诉求的拒绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter is pushed back across the table, still sealed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封没拆封的信被推回桌面另一方。

branches.en: A refused request and a refused person share the same outward motion: what is offered never enters.
branches.cn: 请求被拒与人被拒绝共用同一个向外推的动作：递过来的东西始终没有进门。

branches.en: Manuscripts and faulty goods are literally sent back, so the action also names the object returned.
branches.cn: 退稿与被退回的次品都是实实在在寄回的东西，动作因此也指向被退回的物件本身。

branches.en: In medicine the body performs the refusal internally, which is why transplant failure is called rejection.
branches.cn: 在医学里，身体在内部完成了拒绝，所以移植失败被称为排斥反应。

branches.en: Filters and people alike can keep unwanted input out, extending the word to engineering and social life.
branches.cn: 滤波器与普通人一样可以把不受欢迎的输入挡在外面，于是这个词延伸到工程与人际生活。

branches.en: When the offered thing is a claim or a belief, refusing it becomes an official ruling or a denial.
branches.cn: 当递过来的是一份诉求或一个说法时，不接受就变成正式裁定或公开否认。

intro.en: Rejection is built on the Latin verb reicere, with re- back plus iacere to throw, and the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: rejection 建立在拉丁语动词 reicere 之上，由 re-（向后）、iacere（投掷）与名词后缀 -ion 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere means to throw, and its compounds eject, inject and project all keep the throwing image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere 意为投掷，它的复合词 eject、inject、project 都保留着「扔」的意象。

items.example: Re- marks the direction of the throw.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标出「投掷」的方向。

items.example: Iacere supplies the throwing image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: iacere 提供了这个词背后的「扔」意象。

items.example: Reicere already blends the throwing and the refusing.
items.exampleCN: reicere 已经把「扔」与「拒绝」合成一体。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion turns reject into rejection.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把 reject 变成 rejection。

items.example: Reject entered English before its noun did.
items.exampleCN: 动词 reject 先于名词进入英语。

items.example: Rejection keeps the whole action in noun form.
items.exampleCN: rejection 把整个动作保存为名词。

items.example: The prefix e- gives ejection.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 构成 ejection。

items.example: The prefix in- gives injection.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 injection。

items.example: The prefix pro- gives projection.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 构成 projection。
